summary: Region research direction: mixed — the country's largest LGBTQ+ community and its biggest police raids coexist, with police acting without legal basis. (1) 1 February 2025: police arrested 56 men at a hotel in the capital at a reported "gay sex party"; organisers risk pornography-law prosecution with penalties up to 15 years; Amnesty International Indonesia called the police's "discriminatory and senseless harassment of LGBTI people ... has no basis in law" and demanded release of those detained. (2) One of the eight provinces where an international NGO found discriminatory regional regulations — and simultaneously the city with the country's densest LGBTQ+ infrastructure, media presence and monitoring-group offices; an assessor should expect both to be true at once. National climate from this record's sources: an October 2025 presidential decree listed "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among the country's non-military national security threats alongside terrorism and drugs, amplifying self-censorship (editors killing LGBTQ+ stories for fear of state reprisal); police deny violence and extortions in the 2022 death-in-custody of a US-based trans activist arrested on drug charges at Bali airport while family members allege he was beaten. Model-estimate residual (route 3, best-knowledge delta): sheer scale of the community limits enforcement reach.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 401, paywall); the underlying wire report (Aug 2022) covered Indonesian police denying violence in the death of a US-based trans activist and rights-group founder, 32, who died in custody at Denpasar after an airport drug arrest on his honeymoon; the case's allegations and denials are detailed in the paired article below.

Harvard student newspaper investigation (Sep 2022): mother of Rodrigo Ventocilla Ventosilla, 32, a Peruvian-born trans man and co-founder of a trans rights organisation in Peru about to start graduate study at a US university, says he was extorted (demands up to $200,000), beaten and denied adequate medical care after his arrest at Bali airport (marijuana found in his belongings); he died in custody three days later; local police deny violence; family seeks an independent autopsy; case exposed racism and transphobia in arrest handling. Country-level case (arrest at departure), not capital-specific.

Opinion analysis (Aug 2026): an October 2025 presidential decree named "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" a non-military national security threat alongside terrorism, radicalism and drug addiction; journalists report a constant chilling effect (editors killing LGBTQ+ stories fearing state reprisal or religious backlash); civil-society and independent media space has contracted since 2024-25; documented amid student-led anti-government protests.

tangentialFactors: The October 2025 national security decree framing LGBTQ+ visibility as a threat shapes the local climate beyond what provincial rules do — journalists and platforms self-censor, reducing the public support infrastructure that gender-nonconforming visitors and residents could otherwise rely on.
